# Coding Bible — full agent context

> Complete human- and agent-readable engineering rules for Coding Bible.

Canonical source: https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/
Rules included: 128
JSON contract: https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/rules.json

Use these rules as engineering constraints when relevant. Apply them by intent, preserve documented exceptions, and cite the stable rule ID when reporting a violation.

## Accessibility

### A11Y-001 — Prefer semantic HTML

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#A11Y-001

**Rule:** Use the native element whose semantics match the interaction or content before recreating that behavior with generic elements.

**Why:** Native semantics provide keyboard behavior, accessibility information, and browser interoperability with less custom code.

**DO**

```tsx
<button type="button" onClick={handleSave}>Save</button>
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
<div onClick={handleSave}>Save</div>
```

### A11Y-002 — Keyboard access is mandatory

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#A11Y-002

**Rule:** Every interactive operation available with a pointer must also be operable from the keyboard when the platform interaction supports it.

**Why:** Pointer-only controls exclude keyboard and many assistive-technology users and usually indicate missing native semantics.

**DO**

```tsx
<button type="button" onClick={openMenu}>
  Menu
</button>
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
<div role="button" tabIndex={0} onClick={openMenu}>
  Menu
</div>
```

### A11Y-003 — Keep focus visible

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#A11Y-003

**Rule:** Interactive elements must expose a clear visible state when they receive keyboard focus.

**Why:** Keyboard users need a persistent visual indicator of where the next interaction will occur.

**DO**

```css
.button:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

**DON'T**

```css
*:focus {
  outline: none;
}
```

### A11Y-004 — Controls need accessible names

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#A11Y-004

**Rule:** Inputs and interactive controls must expose a meaningful programmatic name through visible text, a label, or appropriate accessible naming.

**Why:** A control that is visually recognizable but unnamed programmatically is ambiguous or unusable to assistive technology.

**DO**

```tsx
<button
  type="button"
  aria-label="Close dialog"
  onClick={closeDialog}
>
  <CloseIcon aria-hidden="true" />
</button>
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
<button type="button" onClick={closeDialog}>
  <CloseIcon />
</button>
```

### A11Y-005 — Do not communicate with color alone

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#A11Y-005

**Rule:** When color carries status or meaning, provide another perceivable cue such as text, iconography, shape, or position.

**Why:** Color perception varies and may be unavailable entirely. Redundant cues make meaning robust for more users and environments.

**DO**

```tsx
<span className={isOverdue ? "statusRed" : "statusGreen"}>
  <StatusIcon aria-hidden="true" />
  {isOverdue ? "Overdue" : "On time"}
</span>
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
<span className={isOverdue ? "statusRed" : "statusGreen"}>
  ●
</span>
```

### A11Y-006 — Respect reduced motion preferences

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#A11Y-006

**Rule:** Non-essential animation and smooth motion should adapt when the user requests reduced motion.

**Why:** Motion can cause discomfort or make interfaces harder to use, and operating systems expose a preference specifically for this need.

**DO**

```css
.panel {
  scroll-behavior: smooth;
  transition: transform 300ms ease;
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .panel {
    scroll-behavior: auto;
    transition: none;
  }
}
```

**DON'T**

```css
.panel {
  scroll-behavior: smooth;
  transition: transform 300ms ease;
}
```

## AI

### AI-001 — Generated code follows existing architecture

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#AI-001

**Rule:** AI output should use established project patterns before introducing new abstractions.

**Why:** Agents can create parallel architectures and duplicate helpers when they optimize only for the local prompt.

**DO**

```ts
// Reuse the project's established boundary.
const users = await userRepository.list();
```

**DON'T**

```ts
// New parallel data-access pattern.
const response = await fetch("/api/users");
const users = await response.json();
```

### AI-002 — Generated comments must add context

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#AI-002

**Rule:** Remove AI comments that merely narrate the code.

**Why:** Generated narration adds noise quickly and creates stale text maintainers must keep synchronized.

**DO**

```ts
// The legacy endpoint can return stale data for ~30s after account merges.
const user = await userApi.get(id);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
// Set loading to true.
setLoading(true);

// Fetch the user.
const user = await userApi.get(id);
```

### AI-003 — Change the smallest coherent surface

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#AI-003

**Rule:** Do not expand generated changes into unrelated cleanup or speculative refactors.

**Why:** Small coherent diffs are easier to validate, review, revert, and debug.

**DO**

```text
Requested: Fix invoice rounding

Generated diff:
- Fix invoice rounding
- Add the regression test
```

**DON'T**

```text
Requested: Fix invoice rounding

Generated diff:
- Fix invoice rounding
- Rename money utilities
- Move billing folders
- Reformat unrelated tests
```

### AI-004 — Inspect before creating

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#AI-004

**Rule:** Before generating a new helper, component, type, dependency, or pattern, search for an existing solution in the project.

**Why:** Agents can generate locally correct duplicates because they do not automatically share a human maintainer's memory of the codebase.

**DO**

```ts
import { formatCurrency } from "@/shared/currency";

const label = formatCurrency(total);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
// New duplicate helper.
const formatCurrency = (value: number) =>
  `$${value.toFixed(2)}`;
```

### AI-005 — Verify external APIs

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#AI-005

**Rule:** Do not invent package exports, framework behavior, command flags, or platform capabilities from memory when they can be verified.

**Why:** Plausible-looking hallucinated APIs are especially expensive because generated code can appear correct until build or runtime.

**DO**

```tsx
import { useEffect } from "react";

useEffect(() => {
  void loadUser(userId);
}, [userId]);
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
// Guessed from memory.
import { useAsyncEffect } from "react";

useAsyncEffect(loadUser, [userId]);
```

### AI-006 — Do not invent impossible edge cases

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#AI-006

**Rule:** Generated defensive code and tests should reflect actual contracts, trust boundaries, and realistic failure modes.

**Why:** Speculative edge cases bloat types, branches, and tests while obscuring the conditions the system genuinely needs to handle.

**DO**

```ts
function getUserName(user: User) {
  return user.name;
}

// Validate unknown input once at the system boundary.
```

**DON'T**

```ts
function getUserName(user: User) {
  if (!user || Array.isArray(user) || typeof user.name !== "string") {
    return "Unknown";
  }

  return user.name;
}
```

### AI-007 — Run the project's checks

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#AI-007

**Rule:** Generated changes are not complete until the relevant type, lint, test, build, and project-specific validation commands have been run.

**Why:** AI can produce syntactically plausible changes that fail existing contracts elsewhere in the repository.

**DO**

```bash
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

**DON'T**

```bash
# Generated files look plausible, so stop here.
git status
```

## Apollo Client

### APOLLO-001 — Define stable cache identity

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#APOLLO-001

**Rule:** Ensure normalized entity types have stable identifiers, configuring keyFields when the schema does not use Apollo's default ID conventions.

**Why:** Apollo's normalized cache can only merge references to the same entity reliably when it can identify that entity consistently across operations.

**DO**

```ts
const cache = new InMemoryCache({
  typePolicies: {
    Product: { keyFields: ["sku"] },
  },
});
```

**DON'T**

```ts
// Product has sku, but no id/_id.
const cache = new InMemoryCache();
```

**References:**
- [Apollo Client — Cache configuration](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react/caching/cache-configuration)

### APOLLO-002 — Choose fetch policies deliberately

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#APOLLO-002

**Rule:** Use cache-first, cache-and-network, network-only, no-cache, and related policies according to data freshness requirements rather than applying one policy everywhere.

**Why:** Fetch policy is a correctness and UX decision: it controls whether the UI trusts cached data, waits for the network, or persists results for future consumers.

**DO**

```tsx
useQuery(GET_PROFILE, {
  fetchPolicy: "cache-and-network",
  nextFetchPolicy: "cache-first",
});
```

Note: Choose a policy per freshness requirement; this is one example, not a universal default.

**DON'T**

```ts
const client = new ApolloClient({
  cache,
  defaultOptions: {
    watchQuery: { fetchPolicy: "network-only" },
  },
});
```

**References:**
- [Apollo Client — Queries](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react/data/queries)

### APOLLO-003 — Return modified entities from mutations

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#APOLLO-003

**Rule:** When practical, mutation responses should include the modified entities and fields the UI/cache needs to reconcile.

**Why:** Apollo can normalize returned entities automatically, reducing manual cache manipulation and extra network requests.

**DO**

```graphql
mutation RenameUser($id: ID!, $name: String!) {
  renameUser(id: $id, name: $name) {
    user { id name }
  }
}
```

**DON'T**

```graphql
mutation RenameUser($id: ID!, $name: String!) {
  renameUser(id: $id, name: $name) {
    success
  }
}
```

**References:**
- [Apollo Client — Mutations](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react/data/mutations)

### APOLLO-004 — Reconcile mutation results explicitly

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#APOLLO-004

**Rule:** After a mutation, rely on normalized returned entities, update the cache, or selectively refetch affected queries instead of leaving stale client state.

**Why:** Server mutation success does not automatically guarantee every cached list or derived field reflects the new server state.

**DO**

```tsx
await deleteTodo({
  variables: { id },
  refetchQueries: [{ query: GET_TODOS }],
});
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
await deleteTodo({ variables: { id } });
// GET_TODOS may still contain the deleted item.
```

**References:**
- [Apollo Client — Mutations](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react/data/mutations)
- [Apollo Client — Refetching](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react/data/refetching)

### APOLLO-005 — Encode pagination and merge semantics in field policies

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#APOLLO-005

**Rule:** When cached fields require argument-aware identity, pagination, or custom merging, define that behavior in typePolicies instead of scattering cache repair logic across components.

**Why:** Field policies centralize how the normalized cache reads and merges a field, producing consistent behavior for every consumer.

**DO**

```ts
const cache = new InMemoryCache({
  typePolicies: {
    Query: {
      fields: {
        feed: offsetLimitPagination(),
      },
    },
  },
});
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const nextPage = await fetchMore({ variables: { offset: items.length } });
setItems((items) => [...items, ...nextPage.data.feed]);
```

**References:**
- [Apollo Client — Cached field behavior](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react/caching/cache-field-behavior)

### APOLLO-006 — Handle GraphQL errors and partial data intentionally

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#APOLLO-006

**Rule:** Choose errorPolicy based on whether partial data is usable and distinguish GraphQL execution errors from network or transport failures.

**Why:** A GraphQL response may contain both data and errors; treating every failure as identical can discard useful data or display invalid partial state.

**DO**

```tsx
const { data, error } = useQuery(DASHBOARD_QUERY, {
  errorPolicy: "all",
});

if (error && !data) return <ErrorState />;
return <Dashboard data={data} warning={error?.message} />;
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const { data } = useQuery(DASHBOARD_QUERY, {
  errorPolicy: "ignore",
});
```

**References:**
- [Apollo Client — Error handling](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react/data/error-handling)

## Architecture

### ARCH-001 — Separate responsibilities

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#ARCH-001

**Rule:** Rendering, orchestration, transformation, persistence, and external I/O should have explicit ownership.

**Why:** Separating responsibilities makes code easier to reason about, test, replace, and review without requiring knowledge of unrelated behavior.

**DO**

```ts
const orders = await orderApi.list();
const summary = summarizeOrders(orders);

orderCache.save(orders);
renderOrderSummary(summary);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
export const loadOrders = async () => {
  const response = await fetch("/api/orders");
  const orders = await response.json();
  localStorage.setItem("orders", JSON.stringify(orders));
  document.querySelector("#total")!.textContent = summarizeOrders(orders);
};
```

### ARCH-002 — Keep dependencies explicit

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#ARCH-002

**Rule:** A module should receive or import the dependencies it actually uses rather than reaching through unrelated layers.

**Why:** Explicit dependencies expose coupling and make ownership, testing, and replacement easier to understand.

**DO**

```ts
export const completeCheckout = (
  order: Order,
  analytics: Analytics,
) => {
  analytics.track("checkout_completed", order.id);
};
```

**DON'T**

```ts
export const completeCheckout = (order: Order) => {
  app.services.analytics.track("checkout_completed", order.id);
};
```

### ARCH-003 — Abstract after understanding repetition

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#ARCH-003

**Rule:** Do not create a shared abstraction until the repeated behavior and its stable differences are understood.

**Why:** Small duplication is cheaper than a premature abstraction that couples unrelated use cases and becomes difficult to change.

**DO**

```ts
saveArticleDraft(article);
issueInvoice(invoice);

// Extract shared behavior only after the common contract is clear.
```

**DON'T**

```ts
saveEntity("article", article, { draft: true, audit: false });
saveEntity("invoice", invoice, { draft: false, audit: true });
```

### ARCH-004 — Keep side effects at boundaries

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#ARCH-004

**Rule:** Prefer pure transformation logic internally and isolate network, storage, clock, DOM, and other side effects behind clear boundaries.

**Why:** Isolated side effects make behavior easier to test, replay, reason about, and replace.

**DO**

```ts
export const calculateCartTotal = (cart: CartItem[]) =>
  cart.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0);

const cart = cartStorage.load();
const total = calculateCartTotal(cart);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
export const calculateCartTotal = () => {
  const cart = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cart") ?? "[]");
  return cart.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0);
};
```

### ARCH-005 — Keep one source of truth

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#ARCH-005

**Rule:** Do not maintain multiple independently writable representations of the same fact.

**Why:** Duplicated state can drift. A canonical owner with derived views removes synchronization bugs and clarifies responsibility.

**DO**

```tsx
const [items, setItems] = useState<Item[]>([]);
const itemCount = items.length;
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const [items, setItems] = useState<Item[]>([]);
const [itemCount, setItemCount] = useState(0);

// Both must now stay synchronized.
```

### ARCH-006 — Do not add pass-through abstractions

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#ARCH-006

**Rule:** An abstraction should add meaning, policy, transformation, or a stable boundary rather than merely forward every call unchanged.

**Why:** Pass-through layers add files and indirection without reducing coupling or complexity.

**Exceptions:**
- A deliberate compatibility boundary or public facade may justify forwarding when it protects consumers from an unstable implementation.

**DO**

```ts
await fetch("/api/users");
```

**DON'T**

```ts
class HttpClient {
  get(url: string) {
    return fetch(url);
  }
}

await httpClient.get("/api/users");
```

### ARCH-007 — Organize around cohesive domains

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#ARCH-007

**Rule:** Prefer module boundaries that reflect product or business concepts over generic buckets that accumulate unrelated code.

**Why:** Domain-oriented structure keeps behavior that changes together physically close and makes ownership easier to discover.

**DO**

```text
src/
  orders/
    OrderList.tsx
    useOrders.ts
    orderApi.ts
  profile/
    UserAvatar.tsx
    useProfile.ts
    profileApi.ts
```

**DON'T**

```text
src/
  components/
    OrderList.tsx
    UserAvatar.tsx
  hooks/
    useOrders.ts
    useProfile.ts
  services/
    orders.ts
    profile.ts
```

## Core

### CORE-001 — Optimize for understanding

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-001

**Rule:** Prefer code that communicates intent without requiring reconstruction by the reader.

**Why:** Code is maintained and reviewed far more often than it is initially written. Readability lowers review cost, defect risk, and onboarding time.

**DO**

```ts
const activeUsers = users.filter(
  (user) => user.active && !user.suspended,
);

return activeUsers.map((user) => user.email);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
return users.filter((u) => u.a && !u.s).map((u) => u.e);
```

### CORE-002 — Use descriptive names

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-002

**Rule:** Names should communicate the role of a value, function, or module.

**Why:** Descriptive names reduce the surrounding code a reader must inspect to understand behavior.

**Exceptions:**
- Established mathematical notation in a clearly mathematical scope.
- Conventional short names whose meaning is unambiguous in the immediate context.

**DO**

```ts
strategies.filter((strategy) => strategy.goalType);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
strategies.filter((s) => s.goalType);
```

### CORE-003 — Prefer const

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-003

**Rule:** Declare bindings with const unless reassignment is required.

**Why:** Stable bindings reduce the number of state transitions a reader must track and prevent accidental reassignment.

**DO**

```ts
const user = getUser();
```

**DON'T**

```ts
let user = getUser();
```

### CORE-004 — Comments explain why

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-004

**Rule:** Do not narrate obvious code. Document decisions, constraints, and workarounds.

**Why:** Narrative comments duplicate code and become stale. Decision comments preserve context the implementation cannot express.

**DO**

```ts
// Suspended accounts remain for audit history, so exclude only inactive accounts.
const activeUsers = users.filter((user) => user.active);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
// Filter active users
const activeUsers = users.filter((user) => user.active);
```

### CORE-005 — Delete dead code

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-005

**Rule:** Remove unused functions, imports, exports, files, branches, and dependencies when their last real use disappears.

**Why:** Dead code expands the surface maintainers must understand, obscures what is still supported, and creates false confidence that obsolete paths are tested.

**DO**

```ts
export const calculateTax = (total: number) =>
  taxService.calculate(total);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const calculateLegacyTax = (total: number) => total * 0.07;

export const calculateTax = (total: number) =>
  taxService.calculate(total);
```

### CORE-006 — Name meaningful constants

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-006

**Rule:** Give unexplained values a name when their meaning, policy, or unit is not obvious from local context.

**Why:** A named value communicates why a number or string exists and makes policy changes less error-prone.

**Exceptions:**
- Values whose meaning is inherent to the operation, such as 0 when checking an array length.

**DO**

```ts
const MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS = 5;

if (attempts >= MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS) lockAccount();
```

**DON'T**

```ts
if (attempts >= 5) lockAccount();
```

### CORE-007 — Keep cohesive code together

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-007

**Rule:** Place closely related logic together instead of scattering tiny pieces across unnecessary files.

**Why:** Excessive fragmentation forces readers to jump between files to understand one behavior and can be as harmful as oversized modules.

**DO**

```ts
// pricing/formatters.ts
export const formatPrice = (value: number) => { /* ... */ };
export const getCurrencySymbol = (currency: Currency) => { /* ... */ };
```

**DON'T**

```ts
// formatPrice.ts
export const formatPrice = (value: number) => { /* ... */ };

// getCurrencySymbol.ts
export const getCurrencySymbol = (currency: Currency) => { /* ... */ };
```

### CORE-008 — Reduce nesting when it improves clarity

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-008

**Rule:** Prefer guard clauses and early exits when they make the main control flow easier to follow.

**Why:** Deep nesting increases the amount of state a reader must hold in mind. Early exits can make the successful path visually obvious.

**Exceptions:**
- Do not introduce multiple early exits when they make cleanup or transactional behavior harder to reason about.

**DO**

```ts
if (!user || !user.active) return;

save(user);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
if (user) {
  if (user.active) {
    save(user);
  }
}
```

### CORE-009 — Preserve non-obvious context during refactors

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-009

**Rule:** When moving code, preserve explanations and constraints that remain relevant to the behavior.

**Why:** Refactors should change structure without silently deleting historical context that future maintainers still need.

**DO**

```ts
// Gateway may duplicate charges after 2 retries; see PAY-1842.
const MAX_PAYMENT_RETRIES = 2;

export const retryPayment = () => { /* ... */ };
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const MAX_PAYMENT_RETRIES = 2;

export const retryPayment = () => { /* ... */ };
```

### CORE-010 — Keep the public surface minimal

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-010

**Rule:** Do not export functions, types, modules, or abstractions that have no external consumer.

**Why:** Every export becomes a dependency point that constrains future refactoring and increases the surface maintainers must understand.

**DO**

```ts
const normalizeEmail = (email: string) =>
  email.trim().toLowerCase();

export const createUser = (email: string) =>
  repository.create(normalizeEmail(email));
```

**DON'T**

```ts
export const normalizeEmail = (email: string) =>
  email.trim().toLowerCase();

export const createUser = (email: string) =>
  repository.create(normalizeEmail(email));
```

### CORE-011 — Hoist context-free helpers

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CORE-011

**Rule:** If a helper does not depend on its parent function's local values, define it in a stable outer scope.

**Why:** Hoisting communicates independence, avoids needless recreation, and makes the helper easier to test or reuse locally.

**DO**

```ts
const formatCurrency = (value: number) => `$${value.toFixed(2)}`;

export const buildReport = (rows: Row[]) =>
  rows.map((row) => formatCurrency(row.total));
```

**DON'T**

```ts
export const buildReport = (rows: Row[]) => {
  const formatCurrency = (value: number) => `$${value.toFixed(2)}`;

  return rows.map((row) => formatCurrency(row.total));
};
```

## CSS

### CSS-001 — Name styles by role, not appearance

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CSS-001

**Rule:** Class names should describe what an element is responsible for rather than its current visual treatment.

**Why:** Role-based names survive visual redesigns and communicate intent without coupling markup to presentation.

**DO**

```css
.errorMessage {}
```

**DON'T**

```css
.redBox {}
```

### CSS-002 — Use tokens for shared visual decisions

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CSS-002

**Rule:** Repeated semantic values such as colors, spacing, radii, typography, and elevation should come from a shared token source.

**Why:** Tokens keep visual decisions consistent and make system-wide changes possible without hunting through feature styles.

**Exceptions:**
- A truly one-off value may stay local when promoting it would create a meaningless token.

**DO**

```css
:root {
  --color-accent: #34ff6d;
  --radius-control: 0.5rem;
}

.saveButton,
.confirmButton {
  background: var(--color-accent);
  border-radius: var(--radius-control);
}
```

**DON'T**

```css
.saveButton {
  background: #34ff6d;
  border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 8px 16px;
}

.confirmButton {
  background: #34ff6d;
  border-radius: 8px;
}
```

### CSS-003 — Prefer layout systems over manual nudges

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CSS-003

**Rule:** Use flexbox, grid, intrinsic sizing, and normal flow before offsets or spacer elements used only to force alignment.

**Why:** Layout primitives encode relationships and adapt to content, while manual nudges are brittle across font sizes, translations, and responsive states.

**DO**

```css
.toolbar {
  align-items: center;
  display: flex;
  gap: var(--space-3);
}
```

**DON'T**

```css
.toolbarButton + .toolbarButton {
  margin-left: 12px;
}

.toolbarButton:last-child {
  position: relative;
  left: 4px;
}
```

### CSS-004 — Keep component styles scoped

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#CSS-004

**Rule:** Component-specific styling should not leak into unrelated parts of the application through broad global selectors.

**Why:** Global leakage creates hidden coupling where changing one feature unexpectedly changes another.

**DO**

```css
/* RuleCard.module.css */
.title {
  font-size: var(--font-size-heading);
}

.actionButton {
  border-radius: var(--radius-control);
}
```

**DON'T**

```css
button {
  border-radius: 0;
}

.card h2 {
  font-size: 14px;
}
```

## Dependencies

### DEP-001 — Prefer the platform before a dependency

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#DEP-001

**Rule:** Check whether the language, runtime, browser, or existing stack already solves the problem before adding a package.

**Why:** Every dependency adds bundle, security, upgrade, compatibility, and maintenance cost that native capabilities do not.

**DO**

```ts
const uniqueIds = [...new Set(ids)];
```

**DON'T**

```ts
import uniq from "lodash/uniq";

const uniqueIds = uniq(ids);
```

### DEP-002 — Justify runtime dependencies

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#DEP-002

**Rule:** A runtime dependency should provide enough durable value to outweigh its bundle size, API surface, security surface, and upgrade cost.

**Why:** Convenient packages can become long-lived architectural commitments after their original use case disappears.

**DO**

```ts
const shouldAlternate = index % 2 !== 0;
```

**DON'T**

```ts
// New runtime package for one trivial operation.
import isOdd from "is-odd";

const shouldAlternate = isOdd(index);
```

### DEP-003 — Remove unused dependencies

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#DEP-003

**Rule:** Delete packages when no production, test, build, or tooling path still requires them.

**Why:** Unused packages continue to consume install time, security attention, and upgrade effort while providing no value.

**DO**

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "date-fns": "^4.0.0"
  }
}
```

**DON'T**

```jsonc
{
  "dependencies": {
    "date-fns": "^4.0.0",
    "moment": "^2.0.0"
  }
}

// moment has no remaining imports.
```

### DEP-004 — Avoid duplicate solutions

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#DEP-004

**Rule:** Do not introduce a second library for a capability the project already solves adequately.

**Why:** Multiple libraries for the same job increase bundle size, cognitive load, inconsistent conventions, and migration cost.

**DO**

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "ky": "^1.0.0"
  }
}
```

**DON'T**

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "axios": "^1.0.0",
    "ky": "^1.0.0"
  }
}
```

## Feature Flags

### FLAG-001 — Every feature flag needs a removal plan

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#FLAG-001

**Rule:** Create flags with an owner and a planned condition or date for removal.

**Why:** Flags are temporary branches in production code. Without an explicit end condition they become permanent complexity.

**DO**

```ts
export const flags = {
  newCheckout: {
    defaultValue: false,
    owner: "checkout",
    removalCondition: "100% rollout is stable for 7 days",
  },
};
```

**DON'T**

```ts
export const flags = {
  newCheckout: false,
};
```

### FLAG-002 — Delete flags after rollout

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#FLAG-002

**Rule:** When rollout is complete, remove the code branches, tests that exist only for the flag, and the remote flag definition.

**Why:** Completed flags create dead branches and make maintainers reason about product states that can no longer occur.

**DO**

```ts
return renderNewCheckout();
```

**DON'T**

```ts
if (flags.newCheckout) {
  return renderNewCheckout();
}

return renderLegacyCheckout();
```

### FLAG-003 — Keep flag decisions at clear boundaries

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#FLAG-003

**Rule:** Evaluate a feature flag in as few places as practical and pass the resulting behavior or state inward.

**Why:** Scattered flag checks create combinatorial states and make eventual removal much harder.

**DO**

```ts
const pricing = flags.newPricing ? newPricing : legacyPricing;

const price = pricing.getPrice();
const tax = pricing.getTax();
const total = pricing.getTotal();
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const price = flags.newPricing ? getNewPrice() : getLegacyPrice();
const tax = flags.newPricing ? getNewTax() : getLegacyTax();
const total = flags.newPricing ? getNewTotal() : getLegacyTotal();
```

### FLAG-004 — Test both reachable flag states

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#FLAG-004

**Rule:** While a feature flag is active, test the meaningful enabled and disabled behavior that can reach production.

**Why:** A flag creates multiple production paths; only testing the preferred path leaves the fallback branch to rot.

**DO**

```ts
it.each([
  [true, "new"],
  [false, "legacy"],
])("newCheckout=%s renders %s", (enabled, expected) => {
  setFlag("newCheckout", enabled);
  expect(renderCheckout()).toBe(expected);
});
```

**DON'T**

```ts
it("uses the new checkout", () => {
  setFlag("newCheckout", true);
  expect(renderCheckout()).toBe("new");
});
```

## GraphQL

### GQL-001 — Name production operations

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#GQL-001

**Rule:** Give queries, mutations, and subscriptions unique meaningful operation names.

**Why:** Operation names make logs, traces, errors, persisted operations, and refetch behavior easier to identify than anonymous documents.

**DO**

```graphql
query ViewerQuery {
  viewer { id name }
}
```

**DON'T**

```graphql
query {
  viewer { id name }
}
```

**References:**
- [GraphQL — Queries](https://graphql.org/learn/queries/)

### GQL-002 — Pass dynamic values as variables

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#GQL-002

**Rule:** Use GraphQL variables for runtime values instead of interpolating user or application data into operation strings.

**Why:** Variables preserve a stable operation document, keep values typed separately, and avoid fragile or unsafe string construction.

**DO**

```ts
const document = gql`
  query UserQuery($id: ID!) {
    user(id: $id) { id name }
  }
`;

client.query({ query: document, variables: { id: userId } });
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const document = gql`
  query UserQuery {
    user(id: "${userId}") { id name }
  }
`;
```

**References:**
- [GraphQL — Queries](https://graphql.org/learn/queries/)

### GQL-003 — Use fragments for genuinely shared selection sets

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#GQL-003

**Rule:** Extract repeated or component-owned field groups into named fragments rather than duplicating the same selection in many operations.

**Why:** Fragments keep repeated data requirements consistent and make component-level GraphQL requirements composable.

**DO**

```graphql
fragment UserSummary on User {
  id
  name
  avatarUrl
}

query DashboardQuery {
  viewer { ...UserSummary }
  owner { ...UserSummary }
}
```

**DON'T**

```graphql
query DashboardQuery {
  viewer { id name avatarUrl }
  owner { id name avatarUrl }
}
```

**References:**
- [GraphQL — Queries](https://graphql.org/learn/queries/)

### GQL-004 — Validate operations against the schema

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#GQL-004

**Rule:** Generate or check client operations against the current schema instead of relying on hand-maintained assumptions about fields and types.

**Why:** GraphQL's schema can prove invalid fields, selections, and variable types before runtime, making schema-aware validation one of its strongest safety features.

**DO**

```sh
pnpm graphql:validate
pnpm type-check
```

Note: Use schema-aware validation or code generation in CI; the exact command depends on the project toolchain.

**DON'T**

```sh
pnpm type-check
# GraphQL documents are never checked against the schema
```

**References:**
- [GraphQL — Validation](https://graphql.org/learn/validation/)

### GQL-005 — Treat nullability as part of the contract

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#GQL-005

**Rule:** Model nullable fields and variables exactly as the schema declares them rather than erasing nullability in client types.

**Why:** GraphQL nullability expresses real response and input guarantees; weakening or strengthening it locally creates impossible assumptions.

**DO**

```ts
// Schema: nickname: String
type User = { nickname: string | null };
```

**DON'T**

```ts
// Schema: nickname: String
type User = { nickname: string };
```

**References:**
- [GraphQL — Schema](https://graphql.org/learn/schema/)

### GQL-006 — Paginate collections that can grow without bound

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#GQL-006

**Rule:** Do not design clients or schemas around fetching an ever-growing collection in one operation; use an appropriate pagination model.

**Why:** Unbounded lists create unpredictable latency, payload size, memory pressure, and rendering cost.

**DO**

```graphql
query UsersQuery($after: String, $first: Int!) {
  users(after: $after, first: $first) {
    edges { node { id name } }
    pageInfo { endCursor hasNextPage }
  }
}
```

**DON'T**

```graphql
query UsersQuery {
  users { id name }
}
```

**References:**
- [GraphQL — Pagination](https://graphql.org/learn/pagination/)

## Internationalization

### I18N-001 — Localize user-visible text

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#I18N-001

**Rule:** Labels, messages, placeholders, tooltips, empty states, and other user-visible copy should come from the application's localization system.

**Why:** Hardcoded interface strings create inaccessible translation boundaries and are expensive to find after a product expands to more locales.

**DO**

```tsx
import { FormattedMessage } from "react-intl";

export const SaveButton = () => (
  <button type="button">
    <FormattedMessage id="actions.saveChanges" defaultMessage="Save changes" />
  </button>
);
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
import { FormattedMessage } from "react-intl";

export const SaveButton = () => (
  <button type="button">Save changes</button>
);
```

### I18N-002 — Parameterize messages instead of concatenating sentences

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#I18N-002

**Rule:** Use the localization system's placeholders and plural/select features rather than assembling human sentences from fragments.

**Why:** Word order, plural rules, gender, and punctuation vary by language; concatenation assumes English-like grammar.

**DO**

```ts
const message = t("cart.itemCount", { count });

// cart.itemCount:
// "You have {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}"
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const message = "You have " + count + (count === 1 ? " item" : " items");
```

### I18N-003 — Use Intl for locale-sensitive formatting

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#I18N-003

**Rule:** Prefer Intl.DateTimeFormat, Intl.NumberFormat, and related platform APIs for dates, numbers, currencies, lists, and relative time.

**Why:** Intl encodes locale-specific formatting rules and avoids shipping another library for capabilities already provided by the platform.

**DO**

```ts
const label = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
  dateStyle: "medium",
}).format(date);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const label = `${date.getMonth() + 1}/${date.getDate()}/${date.getFullYear()}`;
```

### I18N-004 — Design layouts for text expansion and direction

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#I18N-004

**Rule:** Avoid UI assumptions that only hold for short English text or left-to-right content.

**Why:** Translated labels can grow substantially, and RTL locales invert directional relationships that fixed-width or left/right-specific layouts may encode incorrectly.

**DO**

```css
.label {
  margin-inline-start: var(--space-2);
  min-inline-size: 0;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
```

**DON'T**

```css
.label {
  margin-left: 8px;
  width: 120px;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
```

## JavaScript

### JS-001 — Use async only for Promise semantics

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#JS-001

**Rule:** Do not mark a function async unless it awaits work or intentionally exposes a Promise-returning contract.

**Why:** async changes the function's return contract and error behavior. Adding it without Promise semantics misleads callers and readers.

**DO**

```ts
function getStatusLabel() {
  return "Ready";
}
```

**DON'T**

```ts
async function getStatusLabel() {
  return "Ready";
}
```

### JS-002 — Use optional chaining for genuine nullish access

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#JS-002

**Rule:** Prefer optional chaining when a value may legitimately be nullish, and avoid it when the contract guarantees the value exists.

**Why:** Correct optional chaining makes uncertainty explicit. Defensive chaining on guaranteed values hides incorrect types and weakens reasoning.

**DO**

```ts
const city = user?.address?.city;
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const city = user && user.address && user.address.city;
```

### JS-003 — Prefer default parameters for default inputs

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#JS-003

**Rule:** When undefined should map to a stable default, express that contract in the function signature.

**Why:** Default parameters centralize input normalization and avoid mutation or guard boilerplate inside the function body.

**DO**

```ts
const process = (items: Item[] = []) => {
  // ...
};
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const process = (items?: Item[]) => {
  items = items ?? [];
};
```

### JS-004 — Prefer namespace-safe built-ins

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#JS-004

**Rule:** Use Number.parseInt, Number.isNaN, Object.hasOwn, and other precise modern built-ins instead of ambiguous legacy globals.

**Why:** Namespaced APIs communicate intent and avoid historical coercion or prototype pitfalls.

**DO**

```ts
Number.parseInt(value, 10);
Object.hasOwn(obj, key);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
parseInt(value);
obj.hasOwnProperty(key);
```

### JS-005 — Scope try/catch to the operation that can fail

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#JS-005

**Rule:** Keep setup and unrelated transformation outside a try block unless those operations are intentionally part of the same failure boundary.

**Why:** A narrow catch boundary makes it clear what failed and prevents unrelated programming errors from being mistaken for expected operational failures.

**DO**

```ts
const payload = buildPayload(form);

let result: SaveResult;
try {
  result = await api.save(payload);
} catch {
  showNetworkError();
  return;
}

renderResult(result);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
try {
  const payload = buildPayload(form);
  const result = await api.save(payload);
  renderResult(result);
} catch {
  showNetworkError();
}
```

### JS-006 — Prefer non-mutating collection APIs when mutation is not intended

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#JS-006

**Rule:** Use APIs such as toSorted, toReversed, and toSpliced when callers should retain the original collection.

**Why:** Non-mutating operations make ownership explicit and prevent changes from leaking through shared references.

**DO**

```ts
const sortedUsers = users.toSorted(compareUsers);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const sortedUsers = users.sort(compareUsers);
```

### JS-007 — Use an options object when positional parameters stop being obvious

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#JS-007

**Rule:** When a function has several same-shaped or optional arguments, prefer one named options object over a long positional signature.

**Why:** Named arguments make call sites self-documenting and allow the API to evolve without argument-order traps.

**DO**

```ts
createReport({ data, currency: "USD", includeDrafts: true, limit: 50 });
```

**DON'T**

```ts
createReport(data, true, 50, false, "USD");
```

## Legend-State

### LEGEND-001 — Use useValue for React subscriptions

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#LEGEND-001

**Rule:** In new React code, read observables reactively through useValue instead of relying on observer plus get() tracking.

**Why:** Legend-State v3 recommends useValue for React Compiler compatibility because Hook calls remain visible to the compiler while arbitrary get() calls may be memoized.

**DO**

```tsx
const Component = () => {
  const name = useValue(store$.name);
  return <div>{name}</div>;
};
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const Component = observer(() => <div>{store$.name.get()}</div>);
```

**References:**
- [Legend-State v3 — Migrating](https://legendapp.com/open-source/state/v3/other/migrating/)

### LEGEND-002 — Use peek only when non-reactive access is intentional

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#LEGEND-002

**Rule:** Use get() in tracking contexts when changes should be observed and peek() when the read deliberately must not subscribe.

**Why:** get() participates in Legend-State dependency tracking while peek() explicitly opts out, so the choice communicates reactivity intent.

**DO**

```ts
const userId = session$.userId.peek();
analytics.track("checkout", { userId });
```

Note: peek() makes the intentional non-reactive read explicit.

**DON'T**

```ts
const userId = session$.userId.get();
analytics.track("checkout", { userId });
```

**References:**
- [Legend-State v3 — Observable](https://legendapp.com/open-source/state/v3/usage/observable/)

### LEGEND-003 — Update observable state through observable APIs

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#LEGEND-003

**Rule:** Do not mutate raw objects returned from an observable and then set the same reference back; update the observable node with set, assign, or another notifying API.

**Why:** Mutating raw data bypasses Legend-State notifications, and setting the same reference back may produce no observable change.

**DO**

```ts
store$.profile.name.set("Ada");
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const profile = store$.profile.peek();
profile.name = "Ada";
store$.profile.set(profile);
```

**References:**
- [Legend-State v3 — Observable](https://legendapp.com/open-source/state/v3/usage/observable/)

### LEGEND-004 — Batch sibling updates with assign

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#LEGEND-004

**Rule:** When several sibling fields change as one logical operation, prefer assign over a sequence of independent set calls.

**Why:** assign batches its individual writes so observers update once and the operation is represented as one coherent state transition.

**DO**

```ts
store$.assign({
  data: response.data,
  isLoading: false,
});
```

**DON'T**

```ts
store$.data.set(response.data);
store$.isLoading.set(false);
```

**References:**
- [Legend-State v3 — Observable](https://legendapp.com/open-source/state/v3/usage/observable/)

### LEGEND-005 — Subscribe at the narrowest useful observable

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#LEGEND-005

**Rule:** Prefer fine-grained subscriptions or computed useValue selectors over reading broad trees when only a small value drives rendering.

**Why:** Legend-State's performance model depends on minimizing tracked observables so unrelated changes do not rerender parent components.

**DO**

```tsx
const unread = useValue(store$.notifications.unread);
return <Badge>{unread}</Badge>;
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const state = useValue(store$);
return <Badge>{state.notifications.unread}</Badge>;
```

**References:**
- [Legend-State v3 — Performance](https://legendapp.com/open-source/state/v3/guides/performance/)
- [Legend-State v3 — Tracing](https://legendapp.com/open-source/state/v3/react/tracing/)

### LEGEND-006 — Keep persisted or synchronized state serializable

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#LEGEND-006

**Rule:** When observable data crosses persistence, transport, devtool, or application-specific serialization boundaries, keep that state plain and serializable.

**Why:** Legend-State itself can hold functions and rich values, but serialization layers cannot reliably preserve arbitrary runtime objects or circular references.

**Exceptions:**
- Purely in-memory observables that never cross a serialization boundary may intentionally contain functions or other supported runtime values.

**DO**

```ts
store$.session.set({
  lastSeenIso: new Date().toISOString(),
});
```

Note: Use plain values for observable nodes that are persisted, synchronized, or transported.

**DON'T**

```ts
store$.session.set({
  lastSeen: new Date(),
  onClose: closeSession,
});
```

**References:**
- [Legend-State v3 — Observable](https://legendapp.com/open-source/state/v3/usage/observable/)

## Next.js

### NEXT-001 — Default to Server Components

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#NEXT-001

**Rule:** In the App Router, keep components server-side unless they require state, event handlers, effects, custom client hooks, or browser-only APIs.

**Why:** Server Components reduce client JavaScript and can fetch data close to its source without exposing server credentials.

**DO**

```tsx
const UsersPage = async () => {
  const users = await getUsers();
  return <Users users={users} />;
};
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
"use client";

const UsersPage = () => {
  const [users, setUsers] = useState([]);
  useEffect(() => void fetch("/api/users").then(/* ... */), []);
  return <Users users={users} />;
};
```

**References:**
- [Next.js — Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)

### NEXT-002 — Keep use client boundaries as small as practical

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#NEXT-002

**Rule:** Mark the client entry point that needs interactivity instead of moving an entire page or layout into the client module graph.

**Why:** Everything imported below a use client boundary contributes to the client graph, so unnecessarily high boundaries increase shipped JavaScript.

**DO**

```tsx
// Dashboard.tsx — Server Component
export default function Dashboard() {
  return <FavoriteButton />;
}

// FavoriteButton.tsx
"use client";
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
"use client";

export default function Dashboard() {
  return <LargeDashboardWithOneInteractiveButton />;
}
```

**References:**
- [Next.js — use client](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-client)

### NEXT-003 — Pass serializable props across the server-client boundary

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#NEXT-003

**Rule:** Values passed from Server Components into Client Component entry points must be serializable by React.

**Why:** The React Server Component payload crosses a network boundary and cannot transport arbitrary runtime values such as callbacks.

**DO**

```tsx
// Server Component
return <ClientPrice amount={12} currency="USD" />;
```

Note: Pass serializable data and keep ordinary client behavior inside the Client Component.

**DON'T**

```tsx
// Server Component
const formatPrice = (value: number) => `$${value}`;
return <ClientPrice amount={12} formatPrice={formatPrice} />;
```

**References:**
- [Next.js — use client](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-client)

### NEXT-004 — Protect server-only code from client imports

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#NEXT-004

**Rule:** Keep secrets, privileged data access, and server-only modules behind server boundaries and mark them server-only when accidental client import is plausible.

**Why:** Shared JavaScript module graphs make accidental environment leakage possible; build-time server-only guards turn that mistake into an explicit error.

**DO**

```ts
import "server-only";

export const getUsers = () => db.user.findMany();
```

**DON'T**

```ts
export const getUsers = () => db.user.findMany();
export const apiSecret = process.env.API_SECRET;
```

**References:**
- [Next.js — Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)

### NEXT-005 — Fetch server data directly from Server Components

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#NEXT-005

**Rule:** When code already runs on the server, call the data source or shared server data function directly instead of making an HTTP request to your own Route Handler.

**Why:** Calling your own server endpoint from a Server Component adds an unnecessary network hop and duplicates a boundary that is already local.

**DO**

```tsx
export default async function UsersPage() {
  const users = await getUsers();
  return <Users users={users} />;
}
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
export default async function UsersPage() {
  const response = await fetch("https://my-app.test/api/users");
  const users = await response.json();
  return <Users users={users} />;
}
```

**References:**
- [Next.js — Production checklist](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/production-checklist)

### NEXT-006 — Avoid avoidable data-fetching waterfalls

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#NEXT-006

**Rule:** Start independent server requests in parallel and use Suspense/streaming boundaries when slow work should not block the whole route.

**Why:** Sequential independent requests accumulate latency, while parallel fetching and streaming can deliver useful UI earlier.

**DO**

```ts
const [posts, user] = await Promise.all([
  getPosts(),
  getUser(),
]);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const user = await getUser();
const posts = await getPosts();
```

**References:**
- [Next.js — Fetching Data](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data)

## Performance

### PERF-001 — Optimize where scale exists

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#PERF-001

**Rule:** Prefer readability by default; reduce passes and allocations when scale makes the cost meaningful.

**Why:** Premature micro-optimization obscures code, while repeated work over genuinely large datasets creates measurable cost.

**DO**

```ts
const settingsItem = menuItems.find(
  (item) => item.id === "settings",
);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
let settingsItem: MenuItem | undefined;
for (let index = 0; index < menuItems.length; index += 1) {
  if (menuItems[index]?.id === "settings") {
    settingsItem = menuItems[index];
    break;
  }
}
```

### PERF-002 — Measure before micro-optimizing

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#PERF-002

**Rule:** Use profiling, benchmarks, production telemetry, or a known complexity bound before sacrificing clarity for small performance gains.

**Why:** Without evidence, optimization effort often targets code that is not responsible for meaningful user-visible cost.

**DO**

```ts
performance.mark("normalize:start");
const users = normalizeUsers(payload);
performance.mark("normalize:end");
performance.measure(
  "normalizeUsers",
  "normalize:start",
  "normalize:end",
);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
// "This looks slow."
const cachedNormalizeUsers = memoize(normalizeUsers);
```

### PERF-003 — Prefer one pass on hot large-data paths

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#PERF-003

**Rule:** When processing large collections in a hot path, avoid chains that create avoidable intermediate arrays when one clear pass can do the work.

**Why:** Repeated passes and intermediate allocations scale with dataset size and can become significant in data-heavy applications.

**Exceptions:**
- For small collections or non-hot paths, a readable map/filter chain may be the better engineering choice.

**DO**

```ts
let total = 0;
for (const row of rows) {
  if (isBillable(row)) {
    total += getAmount(row);
  }
}
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const total = rows
  .filter(isBillable)
  .map(getAmount)
  .reduce((sum, amount) => sum + amount, 0);
```

### PERF-004 — Choose data structures for access patterns

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#PERF-004

**Rule:** Use arrays, sets, maps, indexes, or other structures according to how the data is actually queried and updated.

**Why:** An appropriate data structure can remove repeated linear scans and communicate the intended operations directly.

**DO**

```ts
const usersById = new Map(users.map((user) => [user.id, user]));

const rows = orders.map((order) => ({
  order,
  user: usersById.get(order.userId),
}));
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const rows = orders.map((order) => ({
  order,
  user: users.find((user) => user.id === order.userId),
}));
```

## React

### REACT-001 — Keep components focused on presentation

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-001

**Rule:** Move substantial transformation, orchestration, and business logic out of component markup.

**Why:** Separating presentation from behavior keeps components readable and makes logic independently testable.

**DO**

```tsx
const Checkout = ({ cart }) => {
  const summary = useCheckoutSummary(cart);

  return <CheckoutSummary summary={summary} />;
};
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const Checkout = ({ cart }) => {
  const subtotal = cart.items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0);
  const total = subtotal + calculateTax(subtotal);

  return <CheckoutSummary total={total} />;
};
```

### REACT-002 — Do not memoize by reflex

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-002

**Rule:** Use memoization when identity matters or profiling demonstrates a meaningful benefit.

**Why:** Unnecessary memoization adds dependency management and cognitive overhead without guaranteed benefit.

**DO**

```tsx
const fullName = `${firstName} ${lastName}`;
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const fullName = useMemo(() => `${firstName} ${lastName}`, [firstName, lastName]);
```

**References:**
- [React — useMemo](https://react.dev/reference/react/useMemo)
- [React — React Compiler](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler)

### REACT-003 — Keep state as local as practical

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-003

**Rule:** Use explicit props and local state until multiple consumers genuinely require shared ownership.

**Why:** Global state hides dependencies. Local state and explicit data flow make ownership easier to understand.

**DO**

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
// Global store for state owned by one component
const modalStore = createStore({ isOpen: false });
```

### REACT-004 — Do not store derived state

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-004

**Rule:** If a value can be calculated from current props or state during render, derive it instead of synchronizing another state variable.

**Why:** Duplicated state creates synchronization paths and can briefly or permanently disagree with its source values.

**DO**

```tsx
const fullName = `${first} ${last}`;
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const [fullName, setFullName] = useState("");
useEffect(() => setFullName(`${first} ${last}`), [first, last]);
```

### REACT-005 — Use effects to synchronize external systems

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-005

**Rule:** Do not reach for useEffect for synchronous derivation or event handling that can happen directly.

**Why:** Effects run after render and introduce a second execution phase. Keeping synchronous logic in render or event handlers reduces timing bugs.

**DO**

```tsx
const handleSave = () => {
  saveForm(form);
};
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const [shouldSave, setShouldSave] = useState(false);

useEffect(() => {
  if (shouldSave) saveForm(form);
}, [form, shouldSave]);
```

**References:**
- [React — You Might Not Need an Effect](https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect)

### REACT-006 — Use stable list keys

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-006

**Rule:** Keys should identify the same logical item across inserts, deletes, sorting, and re-rendering.

**Why:** Unstable keys can preserve state on the wrong item or force unnecessary unmounts and remounts.

**Exceptions:**
- An index key is acceptable for a truly static list whose ordering and membership can never change.

**DO**

```tsx
items.map((item) => <Row key={item.id} item={item} />)
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
items.map((item, index) => <Row key={index} item={item} />)
```

### REACT-007 — Keep render pure

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-007

**Rule:** Rendering should calculate UI from current inputs without mutating external state or causing observable side effects.

**Why:** React may render more than once, interrupt rendering, or discard work. Render-time side effects become unpredictable under those semantics.

**DO**

```tsx
const UserCard = ({ user }) => {
  useEffect(() => {
    analytics.track("UserCard viewed", { userId: user.id });
  }, [user.id]);

  return <h2>{user.name}</h2>;
};
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const UserCard = ({ user }) => {
  analytics.track("UserCard rendered", { userId: user.id });
  return <h2>{user.name}</h2>;
};
```

### REACT-008 — Move static values out of components

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-008

**Rule:** Constants and configuration that never depend on props or state should live at module scope.

**Why:** Module-scope values communicate that they are invariant and avoid recreating objects or arrays on every render.

**DO**

```tsx
const countryOptions = ["Canada", "France", "Japan"];

const CountrySelect = () => <Select options={countryOptions} />;
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const CountrySelect = () => {
  const options = ["Canada", "France", "Japan"];
  return <Select options={options} />;
};
```

### REACT-009 — Follow the Rules of Hooks

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-009

**Rule:** Call Hooks only at the top level of React components or custom Hooks, never inside loops, conditions, nested functions, or try/catch blocks.

**Why:** React relies on stable Hook call order to associate state and effects with the correct component instance.

**DO**

```tsx
const Counter = ({ isEnabled }) => {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

  if (!isEnabled) return null;
  return <span>{count}</span>;
};
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const Counter = ({ isEnabled }) => {
  if (isEnabled) {
    const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
    return <span>{count}</span>;
  }

  return null;
};
```

**References:**
- [React — Rules of Hooks](https://react.dev/reference/rules/rules-of-hooks)

### REACT-010 — Let React call components

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-010

**Rule:** Render components through JSX instead of invoking component functions directly.

**Why:** React must control component invocation to preserve Hook behavior, reconciliation, and component identity.

**DO**

```tsx
const content = <UserCard user={user} />;
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const UserCard = ({ user }) => <strong>{user.name}</strong>;
const content = UserCard({ user });
```

**References:**
- [React — Rules of React](https://react.dev/reference/rules)

### REACT-011 — Treat props, state, and Hook inputs as immutable snapshots

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-011

**Rule:** Do not mutate values supplied by React or values already passed into Hooks or JSX.

**Why:** React assumes render inputs remain stable for the duration of a render so it can restart, reuse, and optimize work safely.

**DO**

```tsx
const UserName = ({ user }) => {
  const displayName = user.name.trim();
  return <span>{displayName}</span>;
};
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const UserName = ({ user }) => {
  user.name = user.name.trim();
  return <span>{user.name}</span>;
};
```

**References:**
- [React — Components and Hooks must be pure](https://react.dev/reference/rules/components-and-hooks-must-be-pure)

### REACT-012 — Do not suppress Hook dependency correctness

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-012

**Rule:** Include the reactive values a Hook depends on instead of silencing exhaustive-dependency checks to preserve an intended stale closure.

**Why:** Missing dependencies make Effects and memoized callbacks observe outdated values and create timing-sensitive bugs.

**DO**

```tsx
const UserPanel = ({ userId }) => {
  useEffect(() => {
    loadUser(userId);
  }, [userId]);

  return <section />;
};
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const UserPanel = ({ userId }) => {
  useEffect(() => {
    loadUser(userId);
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  return <section />;
};
```

**References:**
- [React — useMemo](https://react.dev/reference/react/useMemo)

### REACT-013 — Extract coherent React responsibilities, not arbitrary line counts

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REACT-013

**Rule:** Split a component or custom Hook when it owns multiple independent responsibilities or becomes difficult to scan, not merely because it crossed a fixed LOC threshold.

**Why:** Small focused units are easier to test and understand, but mechanical file-size limits often create fragmentation without improving cohesion.

**DO**

```tsx
const Dashboard = () => (
  <>
    <BillingPanel />
    <NotificationsPanel />
    <SearchPanel />
  </>
);
```

Note: Split by coherent responsibility, not because a file crossed an arbitrary line count.

**DON'T**

```tsx
const Dashboard = () => {
  const billing = useBilling();
  const notifications = useNotifications();
  const search = useSearch();

  return <DashboardView {...{ billing, notifications, search }} />;
};
```

## Redux

### REDUX-001 — Use Redux Toolkit for modern Redux

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-001

**Rule:** Prefer configureStore, createSlice, createAsyncThunk, RTK Query, and other Redux Toolkit APIs over hand-written legacy Redux boilerplate.

**Why:** Redux Toolkit is the official recommended toolset and encodes safer defaults for immutable updates, DevTools, and store configuration.

**DO**

```ts
const todosSlice = createSlice({
  name: "todos",
  initialState,
  reducers: {
    todoAdded(state, action) {
      state.todos.push(action.payload);
    },
  },
});
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const reducer = (state = initialState, action) => {
  switch (action.type) {
    case "todos/todoAdded":
      return { ...state, todos: [...state.todos, action.payload] };
    default:
      return state;
  }
};
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Style Guide](https://redux.js.org/style-guide/)

### REDUX-002 — Keep reducers pure

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-002

**Rule:** Reducers must not perform async work, generate nondeterministic values, mutate external variables, or trigger side effects.

**Why:** Redux may replay reducer logic for debugging and hot reload; deterministic pure reducers make state transitions reproducible.

**DO**

```ts
markUpdated(state, action: PayloadAction<number>) {
  state.lastUpdated = action.payload;
}

dispatch(markUpdated(Date.now()));
```

**DON'T**

```ts
markUpdated(state) {
  state.lastUpdated = Date.now();
}
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Style Guide](https://redux.js.org/style-guide/)

### REDUX-003 — Keep Redux state and normal actions serializable

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-003

**Rule:** Avoid Promises, functions, class instances, Maps/Sets, DOM nodes, and other non-serializable values in Redux state or actions that reach reducers.

**Why:** Serializable data preserves DevTools, persistence, replay, predictable equality behavior, and debugging.

**Exceptions:**
- Middleware may intentionally intercept a non-serializable action before it reaches reducers.

**DO**

```ts
dispatch(userLoaded({
  loadedAtIso: new Date().toISOString(),
  user,
}));
```

**DON'T**

```ts
dispatch(userLoaded({
  loadedAt: new Date(),
  user,
}));
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Style Guide](https://redux.js.org/style-guide/)

### REDUX-004 — Keep Redux state minimal and derive the rest

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-004

**Rule:** Store canonical source data and derive filtered, aggregated, or presentation-ready values through selectors.

**Why:** Duplicated derived state introduces synchronization bugs and makes updates more complicated than recalculating from the source.

**DO**

```ts
const initialState = { todos: [] };

const selectVisibleTodos = (state) =>
  state.todos.filter((todo) => !todo.completed);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const initialState = {
  todos: [],
  visibleTodos: [],
};
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Deriving Data with Selectors](https://redux.js.org/usage/deriving-data-selectors)

### REDUX-005 — Normalize complex relational collections

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-005

**Rule:** Store heavily relational or repeatedly updated entity data in a normalized shape, typically with createEntityAdapter.

**Why:** Normalization makes entity lookup and single-item updates simpler and reduces duplicated nested copies of the same entity.

**DO**

```ts
const state = {
  authors: { byId: { u1: { id: "u1", name: "Ada" } } },
  posts: { byId: { p1: { id: "p1", authorId: "u1" } } },
};
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const posts = [
  { id: "p1", author: { id: "u1", name: "Ada" } },
  { id: "p2", author: { id: "u1", name: "Ada" } },
];
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Normalizing State Shape](https://redux.js.org/usage/structuring-reducers/normalizing-state-shape)

### REDUX-006 — Use selectors to encapsulate state shape

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-006

**Rule:** Reusable consumers should ask selectors for domain values instead of spreading knowledge of deep store paths throughout the UI.

**Why:** Selectors create a stable read boundary so state structure can change without rewriting every consumer.

**DO**

```tsx
const selectCheckoutCurrency = (state) =>
  state.account.preferences.checkout.currency;

const currency = useSelector(selectCheckoutCurrency);
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const currency = useSelector(
  (state) => state.account.preferences.checkout.currency,
);
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Deriving Data with Selectors](https://redux.js.org/usage/deriving-data-selectors)

### REDUX-007 — Memoize selectors only when they derive expensive or referentially new values

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-007

**Rule:** Do not wrap every direct state lookup in createSelector; reserve memoization for real derivation or stable-reference needs.

**Why:** Unnecessary selector memoization adds complexity without avoiding work, while derived arrays and expensive calculations can benefit substantially.

**DO**

```ts
const selectUserName = (state) => state.user.name;
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const selectUserName = createSelector(
  [(state) => state.user.name],
  (name) => name,
);
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Deriving Data with Selectors](https://redux.js.org/usage/deriving-data-selectors)

### REDUX-008 — Keep transient UI and form state local by default

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-008

**Rule:** Do not put temporary form edits, hover state, or component-local interaction state in Redux without a genuine cross-application ownership need.

**Why:** Local state keeps ownership close to the UI and avoids dispatching global actions for data that is neither shared nor cached.

**DO**

```tsx
const [name, setName] = useState("");

<input value={name} onChange={(event) => setName(event.target.value)} />
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
<input
  value={name}
  onChange={(event) => dispatch(nameChanged(event.target.value))}
/>
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Style Guide](https://redux.js.org/style-guide/)

### REDUX-009 — Use one Redux store per application

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-009

**Rule:** A standard Redux application should have one configured store instance shared through the application boundary.

**Why:** A single store preserves one state graph, one dispatch pipeline, and predictable DevTools/debugging behavior.

**DO**

```ts
export const store = configureStore({
  reducer: {
    settings: settingsReducer,
    user: userReducer,
  },
});
```

**DON'T**

```ts
export const userStore = configureStore({ reducer: userReducer });
export const settingsStore = configureStore({ reducer: settingsReducer });
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Style Guide](https://redux.js.org/style-guide/)

### REDUX-010 — Organize Redux logic by feature

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-010

**Rule:** Keep a feature's reducer logic, actions, and selectors close together, typically in a Redux Toolkit slice, instead of separating the app into global actions/reducers folders.

**Why:** Feature-oriented slices improve cohesion and make the code that changes together easier to find and maintain.

**DO**

```text
src/
  features/users/
    usersSlice.ts
    usersSelectors.ts
```

**DON'T**

```text
src/
  actions/users.ts
  reducers/users.ts
  selectors/users.ts
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Style Guide](https://redux.js.org/style-guide/)

### REDUX-011 — Prefer RTK Query for server data in Redux applications

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#REDUX-011

**Rule:** When Redux is already the application state platform, use RTK Query as the default server fetching and caching layer instead of hand-writing request/cache reducers.

**Why:** RTK Query provides request deduplication, caching, loading state, invalidation, and generated hooks while following Redux's recommended architecture.

**DO**

```ts
const api = createApi({
  baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: "/api" }),
  endpoints: (build) => ({
    getTodos: build.query<Todo[], void>({ query: () => "todos" }),
  }),
});
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const fetchTodos = createAsyncThunk("todos/fetch", fetchTodosApi);

// Slice also tracks request status, cache lifetime, and refetch logic.
```

**References:**
- [Redux — Style Guide](https://redux.js.org/style-guide/)
- [Redux Toolkit — Automated Re-fetching](https://redux-toolkit.js.org/rtk-query/usage/automated-refetching)

## TanStack Query

### TQ-001 — Put every query dependency in the query key

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TQ-001

**Rule:** If the query function changes its result based on a variable, include that variable in the query key.

**Why:** The query key is TanStack Query's cache identity and dependency list; omitting an input can return or overwrite data under the wrong cache entry.

**DO**

```tsx
useQuery({
  queryKey: ["todo", todoId],
  queryFn: () => fetchTodo(todoId),
});
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
useQuery({
  queryKey: ["todo"],
  queryFn: () => fetchTodo(todoId),
});
```

**References:**
- [TanStack Query — Query Keys](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-keys)

### TQ-002 — Keep query keys serializable and deterministic

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TQ-002

**Rule:** Use stable serializable values that uniquely describe the requested server data.

**Why:** TanStack Query hashes query keys to identify cached results; unstable or non-serializable identity makes caching unpredictable.

**DO**

```ts
const queryKey = ["todos", { page, status }];
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const queryKey = ["todos", () => status];
```

**References:**
- [TanStack Query — Query Keys](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-keys)

### TQ-003 — Configure freshness instead of fighting refetch behavior

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TQ-003

**Rule:** Understand staleTime and the default refetch triggers before disabling mount, focus, or reconnect refetching globally.

**Why:** TanStack Query considers cached data stale by default and refetches stale queries at useful lifecycle points; staleTime is the primary control for expected freshness.

**DO**

```tsx
const catalogStaleTimeMs = 5 * 60 * 1000;

useQuery({
  queryKey: ["catalog"],
  queryFn: fetchCatalog,
  staleTime: catalogStaleTimeMs,
});
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      refetchOnMount: false,
      refetchOnReconnect: false,
      refetchOnWindowFocus: false,
    },
  },
});
```

**References:**
- [TanStack Query — Important Defaults](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/important-defaults)

### TQ-004 — Invalidate related queries after successful mutations

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TQ-004

**Rule:** When a mutation makes cached server data stale, invalidate the smallest relevant query-key scope after success.

**Why:** Targeted invalidation lets TanStack Query mark dependent data stale and refetch active consumers without manually synchronizing duplicate server state.

**DO**

```tsx
useMutation({
  mutationFn: addTodo,
  onSuccess: () =>
    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["todos"] }),
});
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
useMutation({
  mutationFn: addTodo,
});
```

**References:**
- [TanStack Query — Invalidations from Mutations](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/invalidations-from-mutations)
