### TQ-005 — Make query functions reject failed requests

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TQ-005

**Rule:** A query function must throw or return a rejected Promise for failures; clients such as fetch need an explicit non-OK response check.

**Why:** TanStack Query determines error state from rejected query functions. Returning an error response as successful data bypasses retry and error handling.

**DO**

```ts
const fetchTodos = async () => {
  const response = await fetch("/api/todos");
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Failed to load todos");
  return response.json();
};
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const fetchTodos = async () => {
  const response = await fetch("/api/todos");
  return response.json();
};
```

**References:**
- [TanStack Query — Query Functions](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-functions)

## Testing

### TEST-001 — Test observable behavior

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TEST-001

**Rule:** Tests should verify a unit's public responsibility rather than reproduce its internal implementation.

**Why:** Behavior-focused tests survive safe refactors and fail when user-visible or contract-visible behavior actually changes.

**DO**

```tsx
openModal();
expect(screen.getByRole("dialog")).toBeVisible();
```

**DON'T**

```ts
openModal();
expect(modalController.state.isOpen).toBe(true);
```

### TEST-002 — Test realistic states

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TEST-002

**Rule:** Edge cases should come from real contracts and failure modes rather than impossible values invented only to increase coverage.

**Why:** Tests for impossible states add maintenance cost while distracting from failures the system can actually encounter.

**DO**

```ts
expect(
  formatUser({ firstName: "", lastName: "Lee" }),
).toBe("Lee");
```

**DON'T**

```ts
expect(formatUser(null as never)).toBe("Unknown");
```

### TEST-003 — Mock the boundary, not its implementation

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TEST-003

**Rule:** Replace external collaborators with the smallest useful test double instead of recreating the library or service inside the test.

**Why:** Complex mocks duplicate behavior, drift from reality, and can make tests pass against a fake system that production never runs.

**DO**

```ts
const paymentGateway = {
  charge: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ id: "pay_1" }),
};

await checkout(order, { paymentGateway });
```

**DON'T**

```ts
vi.mock("payment-sdk", () => ({
  Client: class {
    payments = { create: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ id: "pay_1" }) };
  },
}));
```

### TEST-004 — Test pure logic directly

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TEST-004

**Rule:** When transformation or decision logic has its own responsibility, test it at that boundary rather than only through a distant UI or controller.

**Why:** Direct tests are faster, clearer about failures, and avoid coupling business assertions to unrelated rendering or infrastructure.

**DO**

```ts
expect(
  calculateDiscount({ subtotal: 100, tier: "gold" }),
).toBe(10);
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
render(<Checkout subtotal={100} tier="gold" />);
expect(screen.getByText("$90.00")).toBeVisible();
```

### TEST-005 — Use snapshots selectively

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TEST-005

**Rule:** Prefer focused assertions when the behavior can be expressed directly; use snapshots when a meaningful structured output is expensive to assert piecemeal.

**Why:** Large snapshots are easy to approve mechanically and often obscure which behavior was intended to change.

**DO**

```tsx
render(<CheckoutPage />);
expect(
  screen.getByRole("heading", { name: "Checkout" }),
).toBeVisible();
```

**DON'T**

```tsx
const { container } = render(<CheckoutPage />);
expect(container).toMatchSnapshot();
```

### TEST-006 — Protect fixed bugs with regression tests

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TEST-006

**Rule:** When a bug can be reproduced deterministically, add a test that fails before the fix and passes after it.

**Why:** A regression test preserves the newly learned system constraint and prevents the same defect from silently returning.

**DO**

```ts
it("rejects a coupon at its exact expiry time", () => {
  const now = new Date("2026-08-28T12:00:00Z");

  expect(applyCoupon({ total: 100, expiresAt: now }, now)).toBe(100);
});
```

**DON'T**

```ts
expect(applyCoupon({ total: 100, expiresAt: tomorrow })).toBe(90);
```

## TypeScript

### TS-001 — Avoid any

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TS-001

**Rule:** Use the narrowest correct type instead of opting out of type safety.

**Why:** any removes compiler guarantees at the boundary where they are most valuable and lets invalid states spread.

**Exceptions:**
- A tightly scoped third-party interoperability boundary may require a documented exception.

**DO**

```ts
interface QueryParams {
  page: number;
  sortBy: string;
}

const buildParams = (params: QueryParams) => params;
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const buildParams = (params: any) => params;
```

### TS-002 — Keep types narrow

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TS-002

**Rule:** Model only states the runtime contract genuinely permits.

**Why:** Broad unions and unnecessary optional properties force consumers to handle states that cannot occur.

**DO**

```ts
type Status = "active" | "paused";
```

**DON'T**

```ts
type Status = string;
```

### TS-003 — Use type-only imports

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TS-003

**Rule:** Use import type when an import exists only in the type system.

**Why:** Type-only imports communicate intent and prevent accidental runtime coupling or emitted imports.

**DO**

```ts
import type { User } from "./types";
```

**DON'T**

```ts
import { User } from "./types";

const user: User = getUser();
```

### TS-004 — Treat untrusted input as unknown

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TS-004

**Rule:** Parse and validate external data at a boundary before treating it as an internal domain type.

**Why:** TypeScript types do not validate network responses, storage values, URL parameters, or other runtime input.

**DO**

```ts
const payload: unknown = await response.json();
const user = parseUser(payload);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const user = response.json() as User;
```

### TS-005 — Optional means genuinely optional

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TS-005

**Rule:** Do not mark properties optional merely to satisfy existing call sites or silence type errors.

**Why:** Unnecessary optionality pushes null checks to every consumer and permits states the runtime contract may never produce.

**DO**

```ts
interface User {
  id: string;
  email: string;
}
```

**DON'T**

```ts
interface User {
  id?: string;
  email?: string;
}
```

### TS-006 — Model variants as discriminated unions

**Level:** PREFER

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TS-006

**Rule:** When states have different valid fields, model them as explicit variants instead of combinations of unrelated booleans and optional properties.

**Why:** Discriminated unions make invalid combinations unrepresentable and enable exhaustive handling.

**DO**

```ts
type RequestState =
  | { status: "loading" }
  | { status: "error"; error: Error }
  | { status: "success"; data: Data };
```

**DON'T**

```ts
interface RequestState {
  error?: Error;
  isLoading: boolean;
  data?: Data;
}
```

### TS-007 — Do not cast to silence the compiler

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#TS-007

**Rule:** Use narrowing, validation, or a more accurate type instead of asserting a value into the shape you wish it had.

**Why:** Unchecked assertions can hide a real mismatch between the runtime contract and the type model.

**Exceptions:**
- A narrow assertion is acceptable when runtime invariants are stronger than TypeScript can express and that invariant is documented or proven locally.

**DO**

```ts
if (!isUser(payload)) {
  throw new Error("Invalid user payload");
}

renderUser(payload);
```

**DON'T**

```ts
const user = payload as User;
renderUser(user);
```

## Workflow

### WORK-001 — Run the relevant checks before merge

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#WORK-001

**Rule:** Type checking, linting, tests, build validation, generated artifacts, and other repository-specific checks should pass before code is merged.

**Why:** Automated checks are cheaper and more consistent than asking reviewers to manually detect failures the toolchain already knows how to prove.

**DO**

```bash
pnpm check
pnpm build

# Then commit and update the PR.
```

**DON'T**

```bash
git commit -am "Ship feature"
git push
```

### WORK-002 — Keep changes scoped

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#WORK-002

**Rule:** Avoid mixing unrelated refactors, folder moves, migrations, cleanup, and behavior changes in one change unless the coupling is explicit and necessary.

**Why:** Focused diffs are easier to review, test, revert, and attribute when regressions occur.

**DO**

```text
PR: Add CSV export
- Add CSV export
- Add export tests
- Update export documentation
```

**DON'T**

```text
PR: Add CSV export
- Add CSV export
- Rename utils/ to shared/
- Replace the test runner
- Reformat unrelated files
```

### WORK-003 — Verify usage before deleting code

**Level:** MUST

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#WORK-003

**Rule:** Search static, dynamic, generated, and runtime entry points before concluding that code is unused.

**Why:** Dead-code tools have blind spots around dynamic imports, reflection, configuration, and generated wiring; deleting live code is worse than temporarily keeping dead code.

**DO**

```bash
rg "legacyParser|parseLegacy" src tests config
# Inspect dynamic imports and generated/config wiring too.
rm src/legacyParser.ts
```

**DON'T**

```bash
rm src/legacyParser.ts
```

### WORK-004 — Call out deferred or dependent work

**Level:** SHOULD

**Status:** stable

**Source:** https://xanhast-pf.github.io/coding-bible/#WORK-004

**Rule:** If tests, cleanup, migrations, or dependent changes intentionally land separately, make that dependency visible to reviewers.

**Why:** Explicit follow-up boundaries prevent incomplete work from being mistaken for finished work and reduce accidental merge-order problems.

**DO**

```markdown
## PR
Adds the new parser.

Follow-up: #482 removes the legacy parser after migration.
Depends on: #479 landing first.
```

**DON'T**

```markdown
## PR
Done.
```
